findings.message: The standalone Linux install path pipes a remote script directly into `sh` without any warning or verification step.
findings.rationale: The page tells first-contact users to run `curl -fsSL https://installs.docstube.dev/linux.sh | sh`. Acting on that command executes network-fetched code in the repository environment, but the surrounding text only says to use hosted installer scripts and gives no warning, inspection step, checksum/signature guidance, or trust boundary.

findings.message: The standalone Windows install path executes a remote PowerShell script without any warning or verification step.
findings.rationale: The page gives `iwr https://installs.docstube.dev/windows.ps1 -UseB | iex`, which directly evaluates downloaded code. For an OSS maintainer installing tooling in a repo, the missing warning or verification guidance is security-relevant.

findings.message: The setup-option list is an unmarked checkable assertion about what the wizard presents.
findings.rationale: The sentence says, “During setup, choose the project type, personas, agent provider, information architecture, site settings, theme, and components.” That asserts concrete wizard fields/options but is outside a `<Claim>` marker and was not listed by the deterministic linter.

findings.message: The CLI output behavior is asserted without a claim marker.
findings.rationale: The sentence says, “The CLI reports each generated page, then prints where the site was published.” That is a checkable CLI behavior, while the only marked claim in the block covers the default `outDir` value.
